pull.title: KAFKA-21224: Add mirror-level configs
pull.body:
After broker configs, this patch completes the ClusterMirrorConfig
class. Note: I removed the final "s" from the class name because all the
other configuration classes end with "Config".

Reviewers: Luke Chen <showuon@gmail.com>, Omnia Ibrahim
 <o.g.h.ibrahim@gmail.com>, Christo Lolov <lolovc@amazon.com>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: Thanks for adding the tests. LGTM, Only one minor comment.

I've finished the first round of review. Before approving, I'd like us to resolve:
 - validation for the regex/ACL configs (so invalid values fail with ConfigException)
 - the SASL configs: the PLAIN default, the missing configs (like OAUTHBEARER)
 - splitting the broker-level and mirror-level configs into separate classes

The rest are small nits/doc fixes, feel free to address them here or in a follow-up.
had another round and left few comments! it is getting closer

review_comments.body: Please add tests.
Let's add an `assertFalse` config case.

Why is the default `PLAIN`? The client default, `SaslConfigs.DEFAULT_SASL_MECHANISM`, is `GSSAPI_MECHANISM`.

Correct me if I'm wrong, but I think this could cause a problem once the link is running with `security.protocol=SASL_*`. If the source Admin is created from the raw mirror properties with `Admin.create`, it will use the normal client defaults. Meanwhile, the fetcher would build its channel from `ClusterMirrorConfig`. So if a user doesn't set `sasl.mechanism`, the Admin would use `GSSAPI` and the fetcher would use `PLAIN`. Metadata sync could work while fetching fails to authenticate.

Could we default to `SaslConfigs.DEFAULT_SASL_MECHANISM` instead? `SaslConfigs.addClientSaslSupport(CONFIG_DEF)` would also fix this, since it brings the same set and defaults as regular clients. WDYT?

Another issue I can see; the SASL configs here are only a subset of the client ones: 6 of the 47 configs that `SaslConfigs::addClientSaslSupport` defines. All of `sasl.oauthbearer.*`, `sasl.login.refresh.*` and the Kerberos renewal configs are missing, so `OAUTHBEARER` can't be configured. That doesn't match the KIP's claim that all standard Kafka auth mechanisms are supported.

The SSL set is complete today, but because both sets are copied by hand, they can drift from the client definitions whenever those change.
 
Could we use `SaslConfigs::addClientSaslSupport` and `SslConfigs::addClientSslSupport` instead? That way we keep the same set, types and defaults as regular clients, and it stays in sync when the client security configs change. WDYT?
small nit maybe multi-line comments here better `/* */`
BTW the mirror config in the KIP didn't mention these connection configs. Need to update the KIP to be in line with code

`request.timeout.ms`, `socket.connection.setup.timeout.ms`, `socket.connection.setup.timeout.max.ms` and `connections.max.idle.ms` aren't in the KIP's mirror config table. I know the KIP mentions the source Admin using "network settings" from the mirror config, so I guess these are meant to be covered by that? However, the table lists security configs explicitly (`sasl.*`, `ssl.*`) and some network ones too (`socket.timeout.ms`, `socket.receive.buffer.bytes`), but not these four. I'd suggest adding them to the KIP config table so the full set of supported configs is explicit.

Small one: the doc here is copied from the broker `SocketServerConfigs` one ("server socket processor threads close…"). Since this is a per-mirror setting for connections to the source cluster, maybe something like "Close idle connections to the source cluster after this many milliseconds"?

Small one: this comment says the `replica.*` equivalents use a `mirror.*` prefix, but the keys below drop the `replica.` prefix instead (`replica.fetch.wait.max.ms` → `fetch.wait.max.ms`, `replica.socket.timeout.ms` → `socket.timeout.ms`, …), which matches the KIP. Since these are set on the `CLUSTER_MIRROR` resource, they can't be confused with broker configs anyway. Could we update the comment to say that?

Two small nits here:
- The doc says it's a list of property names, but each entry is compiled as a regex (`compilePatternList` in the constructor). For example `min.insync.replicas` would also match `minXinsyncXreplicas`. That's harmless in practice, but it would be good if the doc said entries are regexes, like MM2's `config.properties.exclude` does ("List of topic configuration properties and/or regexes…"). The KIP table could say the same.
- The doc also says "The mirror.name property is always excluded regardless of this setting", but `mirror.name` isn't in the default list, and nothing in this PR excludes it. Is there a later PR handles that? if so, then maybe add the sentence to the doc there or add comment?
nit: need . before `Internal topics`

General thought here ... `ClusterMirrorConfig` now covers two separate config sets depending on the constructor: `fromProperties` builds a mirror-level config from `CONFIG_DEF`, and `ClusterMirrorConfig(AbstractConfig)` builds a broker-level one from `BROKER_CONFIG_DEF`. All the getters are on the same class, so calling the wrong one compiles fine but fails at runtime. For example, `fetchBackoffMs()` on a broker-level instance throws `Unknown configuration`, and `topicsIncludePattern()` returns null.

Could we split them the way group configs are split? `GroupCoordinatorConfig` wraps the broker config, and `GroupConfig` extends AbstractConfig for per-group configs. For example, keep `ClusterMirrorConfigs` (or a `ClusterMirrorCoordinatorConfig`) for the broker-level configs and use `ClusterMirrorConfig` only for the mirror-level ones. The broker-level constructor isn't used in this PR yet, so now is the easiest time to split it. WDYT?
Let's remove it.
These ought to be just `message.timestamp.{before,after}.max.ms`, no?
This ought to have a REGEX_LIST_VALIDATOR as well, no?

Was atLeast(0) meant to exclude -1? Kafka clients treat -1 as 'use the OS default', which matters for cross-region links. Also, 0 passes validation but makes Socket.setReceiveBufferSize throw. So if we are excluding -1 then it probably makes sense to bump this to 1?

review_comments.body: I also suspect this is meant to stay internal until a later JIRA?
Just to clarify: are these defined with `defineInternal` to keep them hidden until the feature is ready, and then switched to `define`? If so do we have JIRA for this?
Small one: `socket.receive.buffer.bytes` now uses `atLeast(1)`, but clients use `atLeast(CommonClientConfigs.RECEIVE_BUFFER_LOWER_BOUND)` (-1 = OS default). Could we allow -1 here too?
Small one: the doc still says "to the leader for replicating data". Maybe "to the source cluster"?
Nit: this uses the `AbstractConfig` constructor with `doLog=true`, so it logs every config value each time it's built. Should it pass false here?

This list seems to be copied from MM2's `DefaultConfigPropertyFilter`. `message.timestamp.difference.max.ms` was deprecated by KAFKA-14991 (KIP-937), which added `message.timestamp.before.max.ms` and `message.timestamp.after.max.ms`, and then removed in 4.0.0 by KAFKA-17997. Is it kept here so it's still excluded when the source cluster is older than 4.0? If so, a short code comment would help, since the config no longer exists in trunk.
Is this check redundant? I think `MirrorAclRule.parse` already handles `.*` and returns `MATCH_ALL_RULE`, am I right?

Nit: clients define `security.protocol` with `CaseInsensitiveValidString.in(Utils.enumOptions(SecurityProtocol.class))`, so `sasl_ssl` works there, but `ValidString` here is case-sensitive, so the same value is rejected for a mirror. Could we use the same validator as clients?
Yes. https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21231
I'm going to create a custom validator here. Let me know if it is fine.

Nice, your validator is actually more accurate and stricter than client (I would suggest create general Jira which need small KIP to use yours in client at some point). One nit here: since these are plain lambdas, the "Valid Values" column in the generated docs would show the lambda's `toString()` (`ClusterMirrorConfig$$Lambda/...`). Could we wrap them with `ConfigDef.LambdaValidator.with(..., () -> "-1 or a positive integer")`, like `TopicCreationConfig.REGEX_VALIDATOR` does? The same applies to `REGEX_LIST_VALIDATOR` and `ACL_RULES_VALIDATOR`.
Cool. Wrappers are now in place. Thanks.

BTW we should add `mirror.state.topic.min.isr` and `mirror.state.topic.segment.bytes` to the KIP's broker config table, right after to `mirror.state.topic.num.partitions` and `mirror.state.topic.replication.factor`
Are we dropping any thing after the fifth field is dropped without an error or warning? for example what about host ips?
Want to check on last case; wouldn't this fail to pars SSL Principal like for example `User:CN=billing-service,OU=Finance,O=Enterprise,L=London,C=GB`
I did, but forgot to hit update. Now they should be visible.
Update: Yes, we are dropping, but I think we should preserve. Let me think about this.

This is a bug and we need to fix it. Thanks for raising.

In order to keep the compact rules syntax, I'm going to change the property type from LIST to STRING and use `||` as list separator. I'm also going to add the host field, which could be useful for ACLs filtering.

We don't have the same problem for topics and groups lists because the valid chars are restricted, and you can't use commas or pipes.
if this is the case then we should add hint in the config doc for this field that we accept certain number as well

I think extra fields still aren't rejected: with `split(SEPARATOR, 6)` everything after the 5th `;` ends up in the host field, so `TOPIC;.*;READ;ALLOW;User:alice;extrafield;moredata` becomes a host regex that never matches, and the rule silently matches nothing (`testAclsIncludeWithExtraFields` asserts exactly this). Could we split without a limit and reject rules with more than 6 fields instead? Otherwise with silent mismatching users will think they are setting rules that we don't honour.

I think this comment doesn't match what the code does after adding the host field. With `split(SEPARATOR, 6)` the remainder after the 5th `;` goes into the last part, which is now the host (index 5), not the principal (index 4). So a principal containing `;` gets cut off instead of preserved. For example:
```
TOPIC;orders;READ;ALLOW;User:CN=alice\;ops;10.0.0.1
=>   [4] principal = User:CN=alice\        <- principal is cut off
=>  [5] host      = ops;10.0.0.1                <- the rest of the principal + the real host, as one regex
```
The principal no longer matches the real one, and the host regex doesn't match the real host either, so the rule silently matches nothing. If supporting `;` in principals is a goal, I think we'd need some escaping. Otherwise, maybe drop this comment, and splitting without a limit plus rejecting more than 6 fields (as in my other comment) covers it. WDYT?
nit: typo `testAclsIncludeWihWildcardPrincipal` in `Wih` should be `With`

The rule format changing from `||` instead of commas, a new host field, and `*` no longer matches all principals. Those all make sense to me, but we need to update the KIP if you didn't already done that. Otherwise a rule like `TOPIC;.*;READ;ALLOW;*` written from the KIP would silently match nothing.

Wouldn't `TOPIC;.*;READ` work but `topic;.*;READ` fail here, even though lowercase any is accepted? `ANY` uses `equalsIgnoreCase`, but `valueOf` is case-sensitive since the `toUpperCase` was removed. Same in `parseOperation`/`parsePermissionType`. Could we keep upper-casing everything first, for consistency with `security.protocol`? If we do, it should happen before the `UNKNOWN` check, otherwise unknown would get through.

> I think extra fields still aren't rejected: with split(SEPARATOR, 6) everything after the 5th ; ends up in the host field

My bad. See my reply in the following related comment.

> If supporting ; in principals is a goal

Yes, I don't want to put too many restrictions there. I screwed up after adding the 6th filed. Sorry. Fixed by restoring the principal as last field.

In lines 439-444 of `parse` you updated the order to:
```
parseResourceType(parts, 0),
parseResourceName(parts, 1),
parseHost(parts, 2),
parseOperation(parts, 3),
parsePermissionType(parts, 4),
parsePrincipal(parts, 5)
```
This means the order is now `resourceType;resourceName;host;operation;permissionType;principal`. I ran the examples in the doc here through `fromProperties`, and most of them don't work anymore:
```
TOPIC;.*;READ;ALLOW||TOPIC;.*;WRITE;ALLOW  => No enum constant AclOperation.ALLOW
ANY;.*;ANY;ANY;User:alice                  => No enum constant AclPermissionType.USER:ALICE
ANY;.*;ANY;ANY;User:bob                    => No enum constant AclPermissionType.USER:BOB
ANY;.*;WRITE                               => accepted, but host=WRITE, so it excludes nothing
```
The last one is the worst because it's silent. Could we update them to the new order (e.g. `TOPIC;.*;;READ;ALLOW`, `ANY;.*;;WRITE`, `ANY;.*;;ANY;ANY;User:alice`)? Maybe also worth a test that parses the doc examples so they don't drift again.
Same goes for `ACLS_EXCLUDE_DOC`

Makes sense now that the principal is the last field, so semicolons in principals are preserved and we can't tell extra fields apart. Could we just mention in the doc that everything after the 6th `;` is part of the principal?

issue_comments.body:
Thanks @fvaleri for the pr, quick comment the pattern and ACL configs (`topics.include/exclude`, `groups.include/exclude`, `topic.properties.exclude`, `acls.include/exclude`) are defined without a validator, so `AbstractConfig` would accept any string for them. They're only checked later, in the constructor, when compilePatternList and parseAclRules run.

I believe here when a value is invalid, the exception thrown at that point is not a `ConfigException`:
- `topics.include=foo[` throws `PatternSyntaxException`, which is a plain `RuntimeException`.
- `acls.include=TOPIC;.*;REED` throws `IllegalArgumentException` from `AclOperation.valueOf`.

So once the create-mirror path uses this config, a typo wouldn't come back `INVALID_CONFIG`, or the mirror would be accepted and only break later, once the link starts on the brokers.

Could we add validators to these `define(...)`? the same way as `TopicCreationConfig::REGEX_VALIDATOR` in Connect (catching `PatternSyntaxException`)? Each entry would then be checked whenever the config is parsed, and a bad one would fail with `ConfigException(name, value, reason)`, which maps to `INVALID_CONFIG`. It would also name the entry that's wrong. same with rest of regex configs,  and the ACL ones could have a similar validator that calls `MirrorAclRule.parse`. 

WDYT?
@OmniaGM I addressed your comments. Thanks for the review.
@OmniaGM I fixed the bug you found on the ACL rule matching. I'll wait your feedback before updating the KIP with the changes. Thanks.

Thanks @fvaleri for the update. I did another round on the new fixes and left a few comments. The main ones are the extra-fields handling in `MirrorAclRule.parse` and keeping the KIP in sync with the new rule format (`||`, the host field, `*` for principals); the rest are small.
@OmniaGM thanks again. I addressed your comments and updated the KIP.

> @OmniaGM thanks again. I addressed your comments and updated the KIP.

Thanks @fvaleri, the case handling and principal fixes look good. I did another round and left a few comments. The main one is the doc examples, which still use the old field order (most fail, and one is silently ignored); the rest are small. Getting there :)

timeline.body:
Thanks @fvaleri for the pr, quick comment the pattern and ACL configs (`topics.include/exclude`, `groups.include/exclude`, `topic.properties.exclude`, `acls.include/exclude`) are defined without a validator, so `AbstractConfig` would accept any string for them. They're only checked later, in the constructor, when compilePatternList and parseAclRules run.

I believe here when a value is invalid, the exception thrown at that point is not a `ConfigException`:
- `topics.include=foo[` throws `PatternSyntaxException`, which is a plain `RuntimeException`.
- `acls.include=TOPIC;.*;REED` throws `IllegalArgumentException` from `AclOperation.valueOf`.

So once the create-mirror path uses this config, a typo wouldn't come back `INVALID_CONFIG`, or the mirror would be accepted and only break later, once the link starts on the brokers.

Could we add validators to these `define(...)`? the same way as `TopicCreationConfig::REGEX_VALIDATOR` in Connect (catching `PatternSyntaxException`)? Each entry would then be checked whenever the config is parsed, and a bad one would fail with `ConfigException(name, value, reason)`, which maps to `INVALID_CONFIG`. It would also name the entry that's wrong. same with rest of regex configs,  and the ACL ones could have a similar validator that calls `MirrorAclRule.parse`. 

WDYT?

I've finished the first round of review. Before approving, I'd like us to resolve:
 - validation for the regex/ACL configs (so invalid values fail with ConfigException)
 - the SASL configs: the PLAIN default, the missing configs (like OAUTHBEARER)
 - splitting the broker-level and mirror-level configs into separate classes

The rest are small nits/doc fixes, feel free to address them here or in a follow-up.
